subject: BrightAtlas renewal: usage consolidation & proposed capacity increase
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@brightatlas.com>, Grace Chen <grace.chen@brightatlas.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: BrightAtlas usage recap + renewal discussion

Hi Samir / Grace,

Following our Q3 check-in, attaching a short usage report and a draft proposal for capacity options. Key takeaways from the report (attached: BrightAtlas_Q3-usage-report.pdf):

- Total token consumption (Q3): 1.9B tokens — 28% QoQ increase driven by a new summary pipeline.
- Daily 95th latency spike on /chat-infer routes during peak (observed 80–120ms above baseline on 10/12).
- Prefix caching cut effective token spend by ~12% on templated prompts.

We know your renewal is coming up in December. Based on current trajectory, we recommend one of the following approaches:

1) Conservative commit: +25% committed tokens (12mo) — preserves price and adds 10% burst pool.
2) Flexible ramp: quarterly true-ups with an initial +10% commit and negotiated overage rates.
3) Aggressive uplift: +50% commit with a 6mo step-up and an auto-quantization pilot for cost savings.

Questions for you:
- Do you want us to model 12mo vs 24mo economics for each option?
- Are the latency spikes a blocker for you right now (we can pull perf logs for the specific route and timeframe)?

Next steps: we can run a short ROI recap and a proposed contract with SLA credits. I've CC'd Laura for pricing and Ben for any capacity/ops concerns.

Thanks — happy to set a 30-min review this week if helpful.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightAtlas_Q3-usage-report.pdf
From: Samir Patel <samir.p@brightatlas.com>

Subject: Re: BrightAtlas usage recap + renewal discussion

Thanks Monica — useful summary and the PDF looks good. A few quick items from our side:

- We're definitely interested in the uplift; the summary pipeline is mission-critical and we'd rather lock predictable capacity.
- Can you provide a cost per 1M tokens for the Conservative vs Aggressive options (including expected overage cost)?
- The latency spike is a concern: it affected customer-facing flows for about 3 hours on 10/12. Can you share the route-level perf logs and whether a regional fallback would have prevented that?

Grace (procurement) — we likely need a clean 30-day window to review pricing, and a DocuSign for approval.

If you can send a short proposal with the scenarios and pricing, we'll aim to get back within one week.

—Samir
Samir Patel
CPO, BrightAtlas

Subject: Fwd: BrightAtlas usage recap + renewal discussion — ask and pricing options

Ben / Laura — forwarding Samir's reply. Quick internal summary and recommended next steps:

Quoted from Samir: "Can you provide a cost per 1M tokens for the Conservative vs Aggressive options (including expected overage cost)? The latency spike affected customer-facing flows for about 3 hours on 10/12."

Context / Tech notes:
- Their summary pipeline accounts for ~45% of tokens and is highly cache-friendly; quantization pilot should preserve quality for summaries (we've validated on a 200k-token testset).
- The latency spike appears correlated with a regional capacity fallback; ops suggests routing policy + a small reserved headroom for their production region would remove the 95th percentile spike.

Proposed pricing scenarios (draft — see attached proposal-draft-v1.pdf):
A) Conservative (12mo): +25% commit — $0.95/1M tokens base, $1.45/1M overage; 10% burst pool; standard SLA.
B) Flexible ramp (12mo + quarterly true-ups): +10% initial commit — $1.05/1M base; negotiated overage tiers; 30-day true-up window.
C) Aggressive (12mo + pilot): +50% commit — $0.85/1M tokens; includes a 3-month quantization pilot (we expect ~18–22% token cost reduction) and a 6mo staged step-up.

Operations ask: can we commit to a small reserved headroom in us-west for BrightAtlas (target: 2 x p99 capacity buffer) to avoid regional spike? Ops/Ben — please advise cost to reserve headroom.

I will pull together an ROI table for each option if you like; Samir asked specifically for per-1M token comparisons so let's aim to get that to him by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Monica

Attachments: proposal-draft-v1.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: BrightAtlas renewal proposal and next steps

Hi Samir / Grace — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is a formal proposal (BrightAtlas_renewal_proposal_2026.pdf) that consolidates the options Monica outlined and includes:

- Finalized per-1M-token pricing for the three scenarios and an ROI table comparing expected monthly spend vs current run-rate.
- A recommended approach: Option C (Aggressive) with an initial 12-month commit + quantization pilot. Expected net token cost reduction: ~18% on summary workloads.
- Ops commitment: we will reserve a small us-west headroom to mitigate the 95th percentile spikes; this will be included as an operational credit if we miss the agreed p95 SLA.
- Procurement steps: DocuSign link included in the proposal; standard 30-day review.

Grace — let me know if you need an anonymized invoice example for your AP team. If this looks good, we can push the DocuSign today and schedule a 30-min signature handoff.

Next steps:
1) Grace sign-off on pricing/contract OR request one formal change.
2) Monica to kick off the quantization pilot with a 1-week technical readiness call.
3) Ops/Ben to provision the reserved headroom by 11/15 (tentative).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
